meta.name: Inference for Slopes (9.1-9.2)
meta.subject: AP Statistics
meta.description: Unit 9 practice covering population vs sample regression models, sampling variability of slopes, simulation-based inference, conditions for regression inference (LINEAR), sampling distribution of b1, reading regression output, and constructing/interpreting confidence intervals for the slope.

inputs.label: Is the observed slope unusual given the simulated distribution?
Is the population model still valid?
options: Yes, the model is still valid
No, the model is no longer valid

inputs.label: Explain your reasoning:
inputs.placeholder: Use the simulation results to justify whether the population model is still valid...

inputs.label: Interpret the interval in context:
inputs.placeholder: We are __% confident that the true slope...

perField.choiceAnswer: Hint: The population regression model uses all data (true parameters beta_0 and beta_1). The sample regression line uses a subset (estimates b_0 and b_1).
perField.unusualChoice: Hint: Compare the observed slope to the center and spread of the simulated sampling distribution. Is it inside the bulk of the distribution or far out in a tail?
perField.dropdownReason: Hint: Think about where the observed slope falls relative to the simulated slopes. Is it near the center or in the tails?
perField.validityChoice: Hint: If the observed slope is far from what the simulation produces under the population model, that model may no longer be valid.
perField.explanationText: Hint: Mention the simulated distribution center, where the observed slope falls, the estimated probability, and what that implies about the model.
perField.conditionChoice: Hint: The five conditions spell LINER: Linear, Independent, Normal, Equal SD, Random. Match the scenario to the condition it describes or violates.
perField.sdSlopeChoice: Hint: The sampling distribution of b₁ is centered at β₁, approximately Normal, with SD = σ / (sₓ × √(n−1)).
perField.numericAnswer: Hint: Read the SE Coef value from the predictor row of the regression output. Remember SE(b₁) = s / (sₓ × √(n−1)).
perField.lowerBound: Hint: Lower bound = b₁ − t* × SE(b₁). Use df = n − 2 for the t* critical value.
perField.upperBound: Hint: Upper bound = b₁ + t* × SE(b₁). Use df = n − 2 for the t* critical value.
perField.interpretText: Hint: 'We are C% confident that the true slope of the population regression model relating [x] to [y] is between [lower] and [upper] [units].'

tiers.celebrationMessage: Great start! You can distinguish population models from sample regression lines.
Nice work! You understand that sample slopes vary from sample to sample.
Strong reasoning! You can determine whether an observed slope is unusual using a simulated distribution.
Excellent! You can draw valid conclusions about population models from simulation results.
Well done! You know the LINER conditions for regression inference.
Great work! You understand the sampling distribution of the sample slope b₁.
Nice! You can read and use the standard error of the slope from regression output.
Outstanding! You can construct and interpret a confidence interval for the slope.
